question: Which Article of the Constitution of India affirms the right to move the Supreme Court by appropriate proceedings for the enforcement of the rights conferred in Part III of the Constitution?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 32**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 32** gives individuals** **the **right to go to the Supreme Court directly **for the **enforcement **of the **rights conferred **in **Part III** of the Constitution.

 
 
• **Article 32 gives** the individuals the **Right to Constitutional Remedies**.
 
• It gives **individuals** the **right **to **approach **the **Supreme Court** to seek the **enforcement **of other **fundamental rights **recognised under the Constitution.
 
• The **SC **has the **power **to issue **writs **for the enforcement of any of the fundamental rights.
 
 
• The writs are viz. habeas corpus, mandamus, prohibition, certiorari and quo-warranto.
 
 
 
• The **article **is **included **in **Part III **of the Constitution with **other fundamental rights**.
 
 
• The other fundamental rights are viz. Equality, Freedom of Speech and Expression, Life and Personal Liberty, and Freedom of Religion. 
 
 
 
• ** **A **person **can **approach **the Supreme Court directly** o**nly if any of these fundamental rights are violated** **under **Article 32**.
 
• The **right **to **move **the **SC **can only be **suspended **as per the **provisions provided **in the **constitution **itself. 
 
 
• As per** article 359, t**he **right to move any court** for the **enforcement **of **fundamental rights can only be suspended **during a **national emergency**.
 
 
 
• The **jurisdiction **of the **SC **is **original **but **not exclusive **when it comes to the** enforcement of fundamental rights**.
 
 
• It is to be exercised **concurrently **with the **high courts **under** Article 226**.
 
 
 
• Since the **right under Article 32** is in itself a **fundamental right**, the **availability **of **alternative remedies **is** no bar to relief **under **Article 32**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 21 states **that **no person **shall be **deprived **of his **life **or **personal liberty except **according to the **procedure established **by **law**.

 
 
• The **right is available to everyone i.e. both citizens and non-citizens**.
 
• The **right to life** is not **merely confined **to **animal existence **or **survival **but also incorporates** the right to live with dignity** and all other aspects of life that makes the life meaningful, complete and worth living.
 
 
 
• **Article 37** of the **Indian Constitution **deals with the **application of the Directive Principles**.
 
 
• It states that the **provisions of** this **Part **shall not be **enforceable **by any **court**, but the **principles** are **however fundamental **in the **governance **of the **country **and the **State shall ****use **these **principles **while making **laws**.
 
• These **principles **aim to **ensure socio-economic justice **to the **people **and **establish **India as a **Welfare State**.
 
 
 
• **Article 46** states that the **State **shall **promote educational** and** economic interests** of the** weaker sections **of the people particularly that of the **Scheduled Castes (SCs), Scheduled Tribes (STs) **and other** weaker sections**.
